title: Putting Babies On Their Backs Cut SIDS In Half
hook: One free bedtime change transformed infant safety.
closing: Back sleeping cut the risk sharply, but safe-sleep habits still protect thousands of babies.
question: Do new parents know this rule?

segments.say: The SIDS rate fell to 0.64 per thousand births. Back sleeping helped cut the old rate by more than half.
Before the campaign, 85.4% of SIDS cases involved stomach-down placement. Changing that habit targeted the dominant risk.
About 3,400 sleep-related infant deaths still occur yearly. The decline made the rule successful, not obsolete.
